name: App privacy report and Privacy Dashboard
plain: A log in Settings showing which apps used sensors and which domains they contacted.
meaning: Android's dashboard shows sensor access. Apple's report adds network domains.

android.persistence: 24 hours at launch; 7 days from Android 15 QPR1
android.note: Location, camera, microphone; no domain list

ios.prompt_ui: Record App Activity switch in Settings
ios.revocation: Settings > Privacy & Security > App Privacy Report
ios.note: Includes data and sensor access plus contacted domains

limits.headline: Can show you which apps used sensors, and on iPhone which domains they contacted
limits.user_action: You open the Privacy dashboard in Settings, or turn on Record App Activity on iPhone
can: List which apps used location, camera and microphone
cannot: Record on iPhone before you switch on Record App Activity
Block or change what apps do; it only shows a log
limits.differs: Android shows sensor access only; iPhone adds network domains.

story.what_it_is: A log in Settings that shows which apps used your camera, mic or location, and which sites they talked to.

marketing.name: App Privacy Report
marketing.pitch: See how apps use the access you gave them, and which websites they contact.

story.for_you: You switch it on in Settings and then read a simple list. You can see which app used the mic last night and which tracker domains it contacted. It is a way to catch an app that is too chatty.
story.for_makers: The report tells honest apps they will be watched. It also gives a public way to expose bad behavior, since a long list of ad domains is easy to spot. Makers must be ready to explain what their apps send.

use_cases.example: A journalist checks which apps contacted unknown domains.
A parent looks at which apps used the camera on a child's phone.
A free game is found to contact dozens of ad domains.
A privacy researcher compares an app's promises with its network contacts.
A developer checks that their own SDKs do not contact surprise domains.
A person finds that a health app read their location overnight.
IT checks that work apps contact only approved sites.

story.android_note: Android's dashboard shows sensor use, such as location, camera and microphone, with no list of domains.
story.ios_note: Apple's report also lists the domains each app contacted.
